documents.text: The island of Volara is the administrative centre of the Zephyr Archipelago. Its capital city is Thornmouth, which hosts the Archipelago Assembly.
Volara has a population of 48,000 residents and covers an area of 310 square kilometres.
The island of Myrelink is famous for its windmills. The tallest windmill, called the Graywing, stands 62 metres high.
Myrelink's economy depends on wind power. The Graywing windmill alone supplies electricity to roughly 4,000 homes.
Caldera Reef surrounds the volcanic island of Pelagos. Diving season on Caldera Reef runs from March to September.
Pelagos is the only island in the archipelago with an active volcano, Mount Sear, which last erupted in 1911.
The Zephyr Archipelago uses a single currency called the zeph. One zeph is divided into 100 breezes.
Ferries connect the islands daily. The fastest route, Thornmouth to Myrelink, takes 90 minutes by hydrofoil.
The archipelago's national bird is the silver tern, which nests exclusively on the cliffs of Pelagos.
Education in the archipelago is free until the age of 18. The oldest school, Thornmouth Academy, was founded in 1842.
The island of Suncrest grows most of the archipelago's citrus. Its orchards produce about 9,000 tonnes of oranges each year.
Suncrest holds the annual Citrus Festival every October, drawing visitors from across the archipelago.
The archipelago's highest point is the summit of Mount Sear, at 1,340 metres above sea level.
Rainfall is heaviest on Myrelink, which receives about 1,800 millimetres of rain per year.
The Archipelago Assembly has 60 members, elected every four years by the residents of all islands.
Freshwater on Suncrest comes from the Blue Spring, the largest natural spring in the archipelago.
